text:
incident-bot: [P0] Azure northeurope: multiple BGP sessions flap on customer ExpressRoute/OnPrem circuits, detected 1802504321. Automated rule triggered — high error-rate for Private deployments in eu-north. Paging on-call.

tim: Oncall SRE here, acknowledging. Investigating now. @jin can you pull BGP/route table state for the gateway clusters? Also need quick customer impact summary.

jin: pulling BGP logs from the peering boxes. Initial look: repeated NOTIFY and BGP RSTs from two Azure fabric peers. Seen route withdraw/announce cycles for our /24s. Running `show bgp neighbors` now.

maria: Observability: elevated 5xx spikes starting ~1802504200, spikes correspond to p95 latency jump for Private endpoints. Affected customers: 3 with ExpressRoute, 4 with site-to-site VPNs terminating in northeurope. Attach sample metrics:
```
services.private-api.req_5xx_count{region="eu-north"} increased x12
kvcache.miss_rate +18%
```

devon: Customer success: I've alerted account teams for the four enterprise customers with Dedicated+Private. Two customers already opened support tickets reporting intermittent connectivity.

jin: paste: `show bgp neighbors` output snippet:
```
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcv MsgSent  TblVer  InQ OutQ Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
10.12.200.1     4  65515  18234  18234        0    0    0 01:12:34       23
10.12.200.2     4  65516  18234  18234        0    0    0 00:58:12       0  (flapping)
```
Seeing routes come and go for our 10.41.0.0/16-prefixes that host customer tunnels.

tim: Good. What's the immediate mitigation we can do to reduce customer impact? Options: 1) failover affected customers to secondary region routing (if configured), 2) force static routes to preferred next-hop on our side, 3) request Azure fabric restore from Microsoft. Any option take <10min?

maria: We can programmatically withdraw and re-advertise a narrower set of prefixes to nudge session stabilization, but risk traffic blackholing for a short window. We also have short-lived NAT fallback via our regional egress that can be enabled for some customers (non-VPC private endpoints) — that would bypass ExpressRoute.

jin: We're seeing BGP route table evictions due to flapping; re-advertise won't help until peering stabilizes. Re-routing upstream traffic to a secondary gateway in westeurope would require updating route policies — I can push a temporary policy to prefer east-west vpn tunnels to westeurope for affected customer ASNs.

tim: Okay prioritize: (A) enable NAT fallback for the two non-critical customers that can do NAT (maria/devon coordinate), (B) push policy preference to route affected ASNs via our westeurope gateway as temporary failover (jin), (C) escalate to Azure support with BGP dump and ticket. I'll start the incident record.

ops-rotation-bot: tim assigned to incident 2026-INC-482. Next escalation in 15 minutes if no update.

devon: I have the customer lists. Maria, which customers can take NAT fallback? I can message their engineers and get permission.

maria: Customers A and C (internal aliases) can accept NAT fallback for control-plane calls — we'll flip them now. Devon share the outage note: "We are routing control-plane via backup egress while Azure engineers investigate BGP instability in northeurope. No data plane storage changes." Keep it minimal.

jin: Pushing policy now to prefer westeurope for ASNs: `bgp policy import set-prefer route-map FAILOVER-WEST` — applying to edge cluster 3...

jin: applied on edge-3, routes now prefer westeurope. Monitoring traffic shift.

maria: Metrics show partial traffic shift and immediate reduction in 5xx for the customers we enabled NAT fallback for. p95 latency for those customers back to normal. Others still flapping.

tim: I opened ticket with Microsoft: INC# MSFT-221109. Included BGP snapshots, syslog lines, and timestamps. Asked for Fabric team to look at peering instability. Please add any further captures.

jin: attaching traceroute from one edge to customer gateway showing blackhole path:
```
traceroute to 40.77.x.x, 30 hops max
 1  10.1.1.1  0.23 ms
 2  10.12.200.2  * * *  (timeouts)
```

devon: CS update: Customer B reports degraded control-plane for ~18 minutes, affecting some admin APIs. They asked for ETA. I told them we're failing over and engaged MSFT.

tim: Risk: if Microsoft takes >1h to stabilize, we should plan for partial traffic split to avoid prolonged customer impact. Jin, what's risk of route loop or asymmetry if we prefer westeurope? Any customer-visible session resets?

jin: There will be asymmetry for inbound flows during failover but most L7 sessions tolerate it. We might see a small bump in resets. I'll watch tcp reset counters.

sam: Heads up — platform teams: if we move traffic to westeurope, verify capacity for token generation and rate-limited services. I'll pre-check quotas and increase if needed.

maria: Also seeing DNS failed queries for the affected private zones — looks like the DNS resolver path used the same ExpressRoute path and is impacted. For now we can fall back to public DNS resolvers for specific internal records mapped in our resolver policy.

tim: Good catch. Maria, can you coordinate temporary resolver policy to use public resolvers for those private zones as a last resort? Make sure to whitelist only the affected names.

maria: Will do. Applying resolver override for the 4 names we've seen errors for.

ops-rotation-bot: 15-minute reminder: incident 2026-INC-482 still active.

jin: Azure Fabric responded: they've isolated a faulty ToR switch causing BGP session instability in the northeurope POP. Hardware team replacing linecard. They expect 25-40 minutes window to fully restore. MSFT assigned Severity 1.

devon: Passing update to customers with conservative ETA ~40 mins and mitigation steps taken. Customers appreciated immediate fallback work.

tim: Plan moving forward: 1) keep westeurope preference until MSFT confirms stable for 30 mins, 2) keep NAT fallback for consenting customers, 3) monitor DNS override, 4) prepare incident writeup for postmortem. Elaine — you're on next shift; I'll hand over in 22 minutes.

elaine: I can take handoff. Tim add me to the incident record and brief in 15 minutes. Also please dump any remaining BGP logs to the incident doc.

tim: Handoff notes: actions taken, MSFT ticket ID, customers impacted, policies applied (FAILOVER-WEST, NAT-FALLBACK list, DNS-OVERRIDE). Current status: partial traffic shifted, metrics improving, Azure hardware swap in progress. I'll leave it in monitoring and hand to @elaine.

ops-rotation-bot: handover scheduled to elaine in 22 minutes.

elaine: I have control. Acknowledged. I'll keep the incident open until MSFT confirms stable and we have 30m of steady routes. Also will prepare post-incident comms.

tim: Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident 2026-INC-482 status update: mitigated for subset of customers; in monitoring. Last update 1802505987.
